ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: 1) Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (Loi du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme), as last amended by the Law of 27 January 2021; 2) Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant création d'un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), as amended by the Law of 10 August 2023; 3) Grand-Ducal Regulation of 26 June 2019 on the practical modalities of registration and access to the Register of Beneficial Owners; 4) Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as consolidated) and Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies; 5) CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 and CSSF Circular 19/732 on AML/CFT requirements for professionals of the financial sector.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (full access for Luxembourg authorities, the CSSF, the FIU and notaries; restricted legitimate-interest access for the general public following the 2024 Court of Justice ruling in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 that invalidated general public access)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority or civil registry of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Convention (Luxembourg acceded on 30 July 1979) or, for non-Convention states, Consular Legalization by a Luxembourg consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or current company extract of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the corporate shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization by the competent Luxembourg diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate (bulletin n° 3 equivalent) of each proposed manager and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or criminal records authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with certified French or German translation annexed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and confirmation of source of funds for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank, authenticated by the bank's legalization or compliance department
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Banker's customary certification plus Hague Apostille where the signatory's authority requires public authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate of each beneficial owner and corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the country of tax residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn or certified translation into French or German of all constitutive, identity and documentary evidence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's seal and apostille of the underlying original document where required by RCS practice

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, managers and beneficial owners against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC (SDN and non-SDN) lists for USD-denominated letter-of-credit and SWIFT wire payments, and CSSF/FIU advisories; foreign-PEP, domestic-PEP, family-member and close-associate due diligence under Article 3 of the AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) and CSSF Circular 19/732, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, enhanced continuous transaction monitoring on documentary credit and wire payment rails, and mandatory suspicious-transaction reporting to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier, CRF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Commerce and Companies (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), accessed via the eName and eArchives electronic services at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be written in Latin alphabet characters; names in French, German or Luxembourgish are accepted without translation, while names in other languages must be accompanied by a certified French or German translation lodged with the RCS; an SARL must carry the suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' or the corresponding EU legal-form designation from the closed list of Member State equivalents; the name must be distinctive, must not mislead as to the legal form or the nature of the activities, and must not coincide with the surname of a third party unless that party's written consent is produced.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Crédit (prior CSSF banking licence and ministerial approval required)
Assurance / Réassurance (prior Commissariat aux Assurances and Ministry of Finance approval required)
Fonds / Fund / Fonds d'Investissement (prior CSSF licence or approved AIFM/UCITS fund manager authorisation required)
Bourse / Stock Exchange (prior Ministry of Justice and sectoral regulator approval required)
État / State / Government / Grand-Duché (protected state emblems; prior derogation of the Minister of Justice required)
European Union / UE / Euratom (protected EU emblem; prior consent of the European Commission and ministerial approval required)
Université / University (prior accreditation and approval of the Ministry of Higher Education required)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the notary may immediately refile a revised or alternative name through the RCS eName service; for sensitive tokens, a written derogation request must first be submitted to the Minister of Justice or the competent sectoral minister before refiling; an administrative appeal against a formal RCS refusal may be lodged with the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification, must be brought through a Luxembourg-qualified avocat à la Cour, and must state the legal grounds for error or excess of power; an interim suspension may be requested by way of référé where immediate damage is shown; a further appeal lies before the Administrative Court (Cour administrative) within three months of the first-instance judgment.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole office for an active heparin-sodium fractionation business: the Luxembourg Directorate of Health (Direction de la Santé, Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments) requires a licensed physical manufacturing or import establishment in Luxembourg or an approved EU/EEA site with adequate facilities, qualified personnel and good manufacturing practice (GMP) compliance; a virtual office may serve only as an ancillary administrative seat accompanying the licensed operational production site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: quantified 85%–95% probability of unannounced GMP and pharmacy inspections by the Luxembourg Health Inspectorate within the first 12 to 24 months following licence issuance; joint European Medicines Agency (EMA) inspections are probable for cross-border active pharmaceutical ingredient flows; annual RCS commercial substance checks and customs verification of GMP certificates, batch records and supply-chain documentation are expected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 et seq. (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on Accounting, as amended; Law of 10 August 2016 modernizing company law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles of association (acte constitutif / statuts) submitted to the RCS for registration and legal publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum issued share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed; cash contributions must be paid into a blocked account at a Luxembourg credit institution, and the bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) is attached to the notarial deed and released upon RCS registration. The proposed company will adopt EUR 100,000 issued share capital to support the pharmaceutical investment plan.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION 1: The incorporators subscribe in full to the issued share capital of EUR 100,000, payable per the deed, and instruct the notary to obtain the bank blocking certificate evidencing payment of the minimum statutory capital. RESOLUTION 2: The registered office is established at [address], Luxembourg; the board adopts the notarized articles and acknowledges the RCS publication obligation. RESOLUTION 3: The board appoints [Name] as manager and [Name] as deputy manager/authorized signatory, each with powers defined in the articles. The managers are authorized to complete post-incorporation filings with the Luxembourg business registers, tax and social security authorities, and to apply for all industrial and pharmaceutical licences required for manufacture of low-molecular-weight heparin sodium anticoagulant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and pre-incorporation dossier preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS online portal (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify and reserve the intended corporate name (e.g., '[Company Name] SARL') through the LBR e-Register; prepare the draft articles of association, list of shareholders and managers, and declarations of no disqualification; all identity documents must be authenticated and, if applicable, apostilled or legalized.
required_dossiers: Name reservation confirmation from LBR
Valid passport or ID copies of all shareholders and managers
Draft articles of association
Declarations of acceptance of manager(s)
Declarations of non-disqualification for each manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to collision or misleading similarity, file an administrative objection with the LBR or amend the name and re-submit the reservation; the reservation may be renewed for a new period as prescribed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and banker's blocking certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (licensed bank under CSSF supervision)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company 'en formation'; deposit at least the full minimum statutory capital in EUR from the subscriber(s); obtain a formal bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) evidencing the deposit and stating that funds are blocked until RCS registration; the certificate is delivered to the notary.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Identity documents of the signatories and beneficial owners
Draft incorporation mandate or preliminary deed
Proof of source of funds for the capital contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If enhanced KYC queries delay the certificate, provide certified corporate documents and source-of-funds statements; if the initial bank declines, engage an alternative Luxembourg credit institution and re-submit the blocked account application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the draft statutes, the bank blocking certificate, and all supporting declarations to the chosen Luxembourg notary; the parties appear for signature and the notary authenticates the deed; the notary thereafter files the deed with the RCS and requests publication in the RESA.
required_dossiers: Draft deed of incorporation and full articles of association
Bank blocking certificate for the cash portion of the capital
Declarations of no prior bankruptcy or disqualification of managers
Identity documents of all subscribers
Power of attorney, if any, for remote subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies incomplete annexes or legal incompatibilities, provide corrected declarations and re-execute the deed; the notary may issue a supplementary act for corrections before RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the deed and registration forms with the RCS electronically or on paper; the RCS examines the file, assigns the RCS registration number (matricule), and publishes the incorporation in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA); after publication, request and download the certified RCS extract.
required_dossiers: RCS registration form duly completed
Notarized deed of incorporation
Request for publication in RESA
Proof of payment of registration and publication fees
Bank blocking certificate if held by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS sends a query or negative check, the notary must supply the requested documentation within the legal deadline; if the deadline is missed the file is closed and the incorporation procedure must be recommenced with a new notarial act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / corporate bodies / Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the manager(s) formally accept their mandate and file any post-incorporation appointment with the RCS; convene the first manager meeting to approve the opening of bank accounts, adopt the internal AML/KYC policy, and file the beneficial ownership declaration with the RBE; record minutes and retain statutory corporate records.
required_dossiers: Manager acceptance letters
First manager meeting minutes
Beneficial ownership (RBE) declaration forms
AML/KYC documentation for bank onboarding
Certified copy of the RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is queried or refused, verify the ownership data and re-file with the correct constituent instruments; late or incomplete RBE returns trigger fines under the Law of 13 January 2019, so cure immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, municipal, and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Luxembourg VAT (Form 1 / TVA), corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), and municipal business tax; enroll the company as employer with the CCSS; provide evidence of the registered office and RCS identification; use the AEDT portal to obtain VAT and EORI numbers where relevant.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate / extract
VAT registration Form 1
Corporate income tax and municipal business tax registration forms
Employer registration form with CCSS
Bank account details of the newly formed company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT/ACD challenges the registration, respond within the prescribed 15-day period with corrected forms and updated RCS evidence; failure to respond may lead to retroactive assessments or denial of the VAT number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, environmental, and pharmaceutical operating permits initiation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de la Santé (Ministry of Health) — Direction de la Santé, Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments; Administration de l'environnement; municipal authority (commune); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for a pharmaceutical manufacturing authorization and the classed-establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement classé) under the Law of 10 June 1999; submit the environmental impact assessment or registration dossier to the Administration de l'environnement; coordinate with the ITM and the local fire safety service for occupational and fire clearances.
required_dossiers: Manufacturing authorization application with GMP description
Classed-establishment application form
Environmental impact assessment or registration dossier
Site plan and technical installation description
Fire safety plan and emergency response manual
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If environmental or safety objections are raised, amend the technical study and provide supplementary risk assessments to the Administration de l'environnement and the Ministry of Health; an administrative appeal may be filed before the administrative tribunal against a refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Santé (Ministry of Health) — Direction de la Santé, Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments; Ministère de l'Économie / Administration de l'environnement for classed establishments; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for occupational safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation de fabrication de médicaments (manufacturing authorization for medicinal products) and autorisation d'établissement classé (classed installation permit) under the Law of 10 June 1999.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA report generally required for chemical fractionation and extraction of low-molecular-weight heparin crude under the Law of 22 May 2008 on environmental impact assessment, with the facility classified as a classed establishment (établissement classé) under the Law of 10 June 1999; lower-risk auxiliary sites may be subject to registration or a simplified EIA notice.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU; wastewater discharge limits for COD/BOD, suspended solids, heavy metals, and organic solvents per municipal discharge regulations; VOC emission ceilings per Directive (EU) 2016/2284 and best available techniques (BAT) conclusions; hazardous waste consignment notes for EWC codes 18-01 / 18-02 under the Law of 19 February 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the communal fire safety commission and CGDIS (Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps); structural load inspection and certificate of occupancy; occupational health and safety clearance issued by the ITM under the Luxembourg Labour Code; pharmaceutical cleanroom validation and GMP readiness inspection for the heparin API line.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) for corporate registration; official portal: guichet.public.lu and myguichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a Luxembourg national identification number (numéro d'identification / matricule) by filing an application with the ACD through the Luxembourg Business Registers portal. For VAT purposes, registration is made with the AEDT using the relevant VAT registration form (Form 1 for domestic or Form 3 for non-established taxable persons). If the foreign entity has no Luxembourg establishment, it may be required to appoint a fiscal representative for VAT compliance. Tax identification is generally issued within one to two weeks after successful RCS incorporation or its foreign equivalent filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a SARL is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune). Luxembourg resident companies are taxed on worldwide income, with relief available under the participation exemption and double-tax treaties; non-resident entities are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income attributable to a permanent establishment or Luxembourg real estate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg domestic law. Available statutory elections include: (i) optional tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) for resident subsidiaries and their 95%+ owned sub-subsidiaries; (ii) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) election allowing related parties to be treated as a single taxable person; (iii) optional VAT election (option d'assujettissement) for real-estate leases; and (iv) ATAD-related hybrid mismatch elections, limited to neutralising or re-characterising hybrid instruments/entities in accordance with Luxembourg implementation of EU Directive 2016/1164.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €35,000 annual turnover (VAT-exclusive) for the small-business exemption; no registration threshold for a foreign supplier making taxable supplies in Luxembourg; intra-Community distance sales threshold is €35,000 per calendar year; services subject to reverse-charge rules are exempt from local VAT and do not require Luxembourg registration except where validation of a Luxembourg VAT ID is needed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G electronic invoicing is mandatory via PEPPOL standards in Luxembourg; domestic B2B e-invoicing is not a legal requirement; no real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no mandatory tax-authority validation of e-invoice national codes. VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically through the AEDT eTVA portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations may be zero-rated provided the goods physically leave the territory of the European Union within the legally prescribed period and the supplier retains documented proof of export. Services provided to non-EU businesses are generally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the place-of-supply rules (B2B reverse-charge), but the supplier must obtain and retain reliable evidence of the customer's non-EU status. Domestic zero-rating is also available for certain intra-Community supplies to VAT-registered customers when a valid EU VAT number is provided.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document – SAD, or EX-1) or authorised exporter certification
Bill of Lading or electronic air waybill (e-AWB)
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export payment
Transport contract/carrier evidence (CMR consignment note, rail waybill, ship manifest, or freight forwarder confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities can reassess zero-rated export transactions for up to ten years from the due date of the tax period. If zero-rating is incorrectly applied or documentary evidence is missing, the VAT is retroactively clawed back together with late-interest. Fraudulent claims may incur penalties ranging from 10% to 50% of the tax due depending on the degree of intent (good faith vs. wilful deception), and criminal prosecution is possible in cases of fictitious exports or forged customs documents.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) / Central Bank of Luxembourg; the BCL is the euro-area national central bank and the operational arm of the European Central Bank (ECB) for the euro, TARGET2 (T2) settlement and balance-of-payments statistics (VADER reporting). The BCL does not conduct exchange-control administration because none exists in Luxembourg. Supervision of commercial banks, payment institutions and e-money institutions is vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), operating under the CSSF Law of 12 November 2004 and the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, together with the AML/CFT Law of 25 March 2020.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg has full and free currency convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. As a euro-area Member State, the euro is legal tender and there are no exchange controls, no central-bank approval for cross-border transfers, no quantitative limits on payments or repatriations, and no distinction between resident and non-resident for convertibility purposes. Article 63 TFEU prohibits all restrictions on payments and capital movements between Member States and between Member States and third countries, subject only to EU-wide prudential, AML and sanctions measures. Profit remittance is unrestricted in FX terms; the only frictions are fiscal: dividends paid by an SARL incur Luxembourg withholding tax of 15% (0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU/EEA corporate parents; 5%/10%/15% tax-treaty rates for treaty-eligible foreign shareholders; 15% for non-treaty shareholders), interest and royalties generally paid to non-residents are free of Luxembourg withholding tax except in abusive/interest-coverage cases, and no branch-repatriation tax applies. All payments are routed through banks which, under the AML Law of 25 March 2020, must verify the underlying economic purpose. Sanctioned jurisdictions, especially Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria and DPRK under EU Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) regulations as implemented by Luxembourg, are blocked.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement in Luxembourg. The law imposes no timeline for repatriation of export receipts, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to sell foreign currency generated by exports into euro. A Luxembourg SARL may freely invoice in EUR, USD, CNY, CHF or any other currency; may maintain foreign-currency accounts at any licensed bank or, under PSD2 rules, at a licensed payment/e-money institution; and may hold export proceeds offshore or onshore indefinitely. Indirect constraints are limited to: (i) tax accounting in euro for the annual accounts and Luxembourg corporate income tax; (ii) exchange gains/losses being recognised as ordinary taxable income or deductible losses; and (iii) AML obligations requiring the bank to receive a plausible source-of-funds narrative and to perform sanctions screening on the paying party. The liberal treatment results from Luxembourg being bound by the free-movement-of-capital rules of the TFEU and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloque pour attestation notariale) and multi-currency Operational Treasury Account (EUR, USD, CNY, CHF) with SWIFT corporate e-banking, import/export letters of credit, documentary collections and FX/derivatives lines

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Internationale a Luxembourg (BIL) Societe Anonyme

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM (restricted to non-core treasury flows). A Luxembourg SARL may legally open payment accounts with CSSF-licensed e-money institutions (EMIs) or payment institutions (PIs), or with EEA-authorised EMIs/PIs passported into Luxembourg under PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366) and Directive 2009/110/EC. Providers such as Revolut Business, Wise, iBanFirst, Airwallex and Payhawk can execute currency conversion, SEPA, and some MT103-equivalent correspondents, with video-only KYC. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs may not grant credit, issue or confirm letters of credit; (ii) client funds are safeguarded in segregated accounts consistent with EMIR/financial-services safeguarding rules; (iii) transaction/volume limits and refusal rights are common for pharmaceutical trade, especially with Chinese/US counterparties; (iv) no MT700 documentary credit capability; (v) digital-only onboarding is accepted, but on later EDD the EMI may require physical documents and bank references, and may freeze mid-size flows pending proof of trade. Conclusion: an EMI is viable only for marginal FX conversion and supplier payments below EUR 50,000, not for the SARL's core LC/SWIFT treasury. BGL BNP Paribas or BIL remain the anchor banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Luxembourg's AML Law of 25 March 2020 and CSSF circulars, the SARL's signatories, legal representatives and all beneficial owners (any natural person holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of share capital or control) must be identified through face-to-face or, in exceptional cases, authenticated remote means. In practical bank policy, at least one director or authorised signatory must physically appear at the Luxembourg branch for an initial KYC interview to validate the signature card and beneficial-ownership declaration. Non-resident directors may alternatively: (i) grant a power of attorney to a Luxembourg-resident manager (mandataire) who appears in person; (ii) submit certified copies of passport with apostille and a sworn source-of-funds statement, translated into French/German/English as the bank requests; and (iii) attend a live video-identity conference with the compliance officer. Pure remote onboarding with no personal appearance is generally refused for a medium-risk 'Active Pharma Extraction' SARL because of the high-value cross-border wire and LC activity. The bank will also request the original notarial deed (statuts), the RCS extract, the RBE beneficial-ownership filing proof, and a projected cash-flow/business plan covering the heparin sodium trade cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or non-transparent ownership chain, with a foreign parent or UBO located in a FATF grey/black-listed jurisdiction or a low-tax intermediate holding, causing automatic enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder organigram to the ultimate natural-person UBO; RCS extract; RBE beneficial-ownership certificate; notarised and apostilled certified passport copies of all directors/UBOs; source-of-wealth statement per UBO (employment, dividends, sale contracts, audited financials); three years of audited shareholder accounts; home-bank reference letter; written commercial rationale for the Luxembourg holding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk biological pharma supply chain: heparin sodium is an active substance of porcine origin, with concentrated Chinese crude-heparin processors, raising concerns about authenticity, cold-chain integrity and product contamination.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg Ministry of Health (Direction de la Sante) authorisation for manufacturing/wholesale of active substances; EU GMP certificate of the extraction facility; ISO 9001 and environmental/quality certifications; veterinary health certificates and EU import-condition compliance under Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009 and Regulation (EU) No 142/2011; supply-chain traceability map from licensed slaughterhouses to crude processors; lot-specific Certificates of Analysis; recent buyer audit reports; and the qualified-person release protocol.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Back-to-back trade and third-party payments: letters of credit, settlement through Hong Kong/Singapore intermediary accounts, or any invoice settled by a party different from the contractual counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Final sale and purchase agreements with Incoterms 2020; per-shipment document set (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/AWB, insurance certificate, CoA, GMP certificate, certificate of origin, customs SAD declarations); title-transmission evidence; incoming/outgoing SWIFT matching reconciliation; a board policy prohibiting third-party settlement without prior compliance approval; and proof of ultimate consignee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/embargo exposure: US or EU sanctioned jurisdictions in the trade route, any vessel/shipowner or beneficial owner matching SDN/EU/UK/HMT lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions screening outputs against EU, UN, OFAC SDN and UK HMT lists for all counterparties and vessels before each shipment; internal export-compliance manual; board confirmation that heparin sodium is not a dual-use/ITAR/EAR controlled item; end-user attestations; transport documents showing final discharge ports; and for false-positive name matches, a negative-verification memo containing passport/registration/address evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Luxembourg SARL the statutory minimum share capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation. The founders must open a blocked escrow account ('compte bloque') at a Luxembourg bank in the name of the company in formation; the bank issues an attestation de blocage (capital-release certificate) on which the notary relies when authenticating the articles of association. The compliant wire protocol is: (1) the founding shareholder instructs its non-resident bank to send a SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA/T2 message where both parties are in EEA) in euro to the escrow account, using the IBAN starting with LU and the Luxembourg BIC; (2) the payment reference must include the words 'versement du capital social - constitution LU_SARL' (share capital subscription) and the shareholder's name; (3) if the sending bank requires a balance-of-payments/ECB purpose code, the correct classification is 'equity capital - inward direct investment' in the direct-investment enterprise; (4) the remittance must originate from the subscribing shareholder's own account, never from a third party; (5) the Luxembourg bank performs source-of-funds verification and may request a source-of-funds memorandum, certified shareholder resolution and audited financials; (6) at notarial deed signing the escrow account is released and becomes the operational account (or is transferred to it upon RCS registration); (7) capital increases follow the same MT103 rail with a notarial/shareholders resolution and updated ECB/BCL direct-investment reporting. Ecuadorian? Not applicable. Inbound non-EU capital requires no Luxembourg exchange-control permit; only the bank's ordinary AML/KYC analysis and BCL external-statistics reporting apply. ESG? No additional licence except the underlying business licence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The principal clearing rails, in ranked suitability: (i) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for open-account settlements and intercompany treasury transactions; EUR legs clear via TARGET2/SEPA, USD legs via the Luxembourg bank's New York correspondent on Fedwire/CHIPS, and offshore CNY/CNH via CNH-clearing banks; (ii) irrevocable commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) advised and, where required, confirmed by BGL BNP Paribas or BIL for high-value heparin sodium deliveries; the standard presentation includes draft, commercial invoice, packing list, full-set original transport document, endorsed insurance policy, Certificate of Analysis, batch release certificate, GMP certificate, certificate of origin and veterinary/competent-authority health certificates; (iii) for crude-heparin raw-material imports from China, sight or 90-day usance LCs payable against presentation, supplemented by third-party quality inspection certificates (SGS/Cotecna) and veterinary certificates; (iv) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) as fallback where the bank does not extend LC limits; and (v) T2/SEPA credit transfers for payroll, VAT, corporate income tax and utility disbursements. All outbound USD payments are subject to OFAC screening through the US correspondent; EU/UN sanctions screening is performed automatically at the Luxembourg bank. The SARL should include its LEI (549300LUX) in CBPR+ structured fields where possible and maintain a full audit trail linking each MT103 to the underlying invoice, customs declaration, and supply contract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court fine up to EUR 5,000; persistent failure may trigger judicial dissolution/administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit required if the SARL exceeds two of the three following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 3,650,000; net turnover EUR 7,300,000; average headcount 50. Mandatory in any case for public-interest entities, financial undertakings, or if the articles of incorporation require it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register, as amended); IFRS may be applied as an alternative for statutory annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any shareholding transfer or other change in beneficial ownership must be filed with the RBE within 30 days. In addition, all UBO data must be re-confirmed annually by 31 March of each calendar year, even in the absence of changes. The register of members must be updated simultaneously.
